candidate.version_description: This song has been played my numerous artists, each adding their own word changes but built a round a central theme. I heard this version back in the '60's and it's unique in that it adds a second line to the refain lamenting the worry his girfriend has left him for another, thus giving a reason for his journey home.

content:
Played either finger picking or flat picking style.


[Verse 1]

[tab][ch]Am[/ch]
Well I'm walkin' down the track,[/tab]

I got tears in my eyes
[tab]                                [ch]E7[/ch]
Tryin' to read a letter from my home.[/tab]
[tab]        [ch]Am[/ch]
If that train runs me right,[/tab]

I'll be home tomorrow night
[tab]                        [ch]E7[/ch]            [ch]Am[/ch]
'Cause I'm nine hundred miles from my home.[/tab]
